To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the quality of investor protections is positively related to firm growth, and that the quality of corporate governance is positively related to the level of firm risk taking.

(1) the quality of corporate governance and investor protection is positively correlated with corporate risk taking; (2) the positive correlation between the quality of investor governance and corporate risk taking holds for the United States, but not for other developed countries; (3) the positive correlation holds for firms with a large proportion of institutional investors, but not for firms with a high proportion of family or founder ownership; and (4) the positive correlation is stronger for firms with high growth opportunities.
(1) better investor protection leads to higher corporate risk taking and (2) the positive relation between investor protection and corporate risk taking is more pronounced for growth firms.
